tool_summary: Changes file mode (permission) bits. World-writable or setuid/setgid modes are common security misconfigurations, and -R applies a mode change across an entire directory tree at once.
platform_notes: Core numeric and symbolic mode syntax (-R, -r/-h) is consistent between GNU and BSD chmod; some symbolic/numeric edge cases and -h (act on symlink itself) behavior differ subtly, but not for the flags covered here.

rules.description: A numeric mode with the setuid or setgid bit set (e.g. 4755, 2755, or symbolic u+s/g+s) causes the file to execute with the file owner's or group's privileges regardless of who runs it. This is a classic privilege escalation vector if the owner is root.

Recursive application of a world-writable mode (777, a+w, o+w) makes an entire directory tree writable by any user on the system, which can be used to plant or tamper with files, or as a staging area for further compromise.
rules.notes: The raw_pattern is a best-effort heuristic covering flag-before-mode and mode-before-flag orderings; it will not catch every possible token arrangement (e.g. additional interleaved flags like -Rv 777) since it is not a full command-line parse. flags_any: [-R] alone still ensures chmod-recursive fires as a fallback in those cases.

rules.description: Applying a world-writable mode (777, a+w, o+w) makes a file writable by any user on the system.

Recursively applies a mode change across an entire directory tree at once. This is worth attention independent of privilege level: recursion is inherently harder to scope correctly (a mistaken path, an unexpected symlink, or a broader tree than intended can all be affected), and neither commandant nor chmod itself records the prior mode to allow a clean undo. Combined with -L/-H (dereference symlinks), can also affect files outside the target directory if symlinks point elsewhere.
rules.reversible_note: Neither chmod nor commandant records the prior mode of affected files, so a recursive change cannot be cleanly undone without separately-recorded state.
